::: {.lead}
I study how the digital traces students leave in online learning environments can be turned into meaningful, theory-informed evidence about *how* they learn, so that educators can see and support self-regulated learning as it happens.

## Current project

::: {.project-card}
[PhD research · The University of Western Australia · 2020–present]{.project-meta}

### A systematic framework for context- and domain-driven event abstraction in multi-modal data within online collaborative learning environments

Learning platforms record every click, submission and forum post, but these low-level events say little on their own about whether a student is planning, monitoring or reflecting. My doctoral research develops a framework that abstracts raw, multi-modal event logs into high-level **learning actions** grounded in self-regulated learning (SRL) theory and the course context. The resulting action sequences are analysed with process mining to reveal how students regulate their learning over time, and are validated through expert judgement.

::: {.pipeline}
::: {.step}
**Raw event logs**\
LMS, forums, code repositories
:::
::: {.step .step-key}
**Event abstraction**\
context and domain rules
:::
::: {.step}
**Learning actions**\
mapped to SRL phases
:::
::: {.step}
**Process mining**\
sequences and patterns
:::
::: {.step}
**Insight for educators**\
feedback and nudges
:::
:::

**Research questions**

1. How can low-level learning events be abstracted into learning actions that are meaningful from an SRL perspective?
2. How can course context and domain knowledge guide that abstraction across different learning environments?
3. What do the resulting process models reveal about how students regulate their learning in collaborative online settings?

## Research themes and publications

Each paper links to its source through its DOI or publisher page; the **Scholar** link finds free versions and citing work.

### Self-regulated learning & learning design {#theme-srl}

How students plan, monitor and reflect on their learning, how to measure it, and how course design in blended and online settings supports it.

:::{#papers-srl}
:::

### Educational data mining & process mining {#theme-edm}

Predicting study outcomes, graduation and specialisation fit from academic records, and analysing academic processes from event logs.

:::{#papers-edm}
:::

### Text mining & sentiment analysis {#theme-text}

Classifying exam questions by cognitive level and analysing public opinion in reviews and social media.

:::{#papers-text}
:::

### Data quality management {#theme-dq}

Data profiling, cleansing and monitoring with open-source tools, applied in government agencies.

:::{#papers-dq}
:::

### Information systems & digital society {#theme-is}

Enterprise systems readiness, smart-society platforms and mobile applications for campus and community services.

:::{#papers-is}
:::

## Collaboration

I welcome collaboration on learning analytics, self-regulated learning and process mining in education, and I supervise undergraduate research in these areas at Telkom University. See my [CV](cv.qmd) for background, or get in touch through the links on the [About](index.qmd) page.
